meta.parties: Suppramaniam Et Al. v. Erampakurukal Et Al

rules.statement: An heir who acquires rights by operation of law, such as through intestate succession, is not considered a purchaser for value and cannot claim priority over the original fraudulent transaction.
rules.supporting_quote: "There is no evidence to support a finding that the second petitioner was in any manner a party to the fraud of her father. It must, therefore, be assumed that so far as her own acts are concerned, she is innocent of any fraud. But her innocence does not help her. She is a mere volunteer so far as the devolution of the right under the otty deed is concerned, for she acquired those rights by operation of the law of intestate succession, and was therefore not a purchaser for value."
